newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE WILL MEET EMU CRITERIA IN 99 - KARATZAS.
newsitem.headline: GREECE WILL MEET EMU CRITERIA IN 99 - KARATZAS.

text.p: Greece's economy will meet the Maastricht criteria in 1999 at the latest provided that the government sticks to the EU-approved convergence plan, said Theodore Karatzas, chairman of the country's largest commercial bank, National Bank of Greece .

"If the government continues to adhere to the EU approved convergence plan and I think it will do so, the Greek economy will fulfill the Maastricht criteria in 1999 at the latest," said Karatzas who called the EMU process "irreversible".
Consumer price inflation fell to 5.4 percent year-on-year in May from 5.9 percent in April but government officials and other economists expect limited progress in slowing down inflation by end-97.
"We should not be impressed by seasonal fluctuations in inflation. What counts is the trend and this points downwards," he said. "The course of inflation is not linear."
The National Bank chairman said he favoured gradualism as an approach in tackling structural problems such as the ailing social insurance system and labour market which warranted painful measures.
He called the recent fall of the Athens bourse "temporary" but declined to say where he saw the general share index at the end of 1997.
"The course of the Athens stock exchange will be positive," said Karatzas who has in the past headed committees responsible for the deregulation and modernisation of Greece's capital market.
The chairman of the National Bank said his bank pursued a new strategy aiming at becoming a major regional player in Southeastern Europe with a presence in all major financial centres.

"The old strategy of the bank was to follow Greek immigrants around the globe but the new strategy aims at strengthening its presence in all major international financial centres and becoming a major player in Southeastern Europe and the Middle East," he said.
National Bank was also mobilising all of its resources in Greece to become more competitive and profitable in the new, more demanding local banking landscape.
"It takes some time for the new message to spread out from the top to the bottom but the signals we get are encouraging," said Karatzas. "When there is a will, there is a way."
He declined to say anything more about the first-half results of the National Bank other than "they will be better than last year's"
National Bank's first-quarter earnings rose 80 percent to 19.7 billion drachmas this year compared to the same period a year ago, a high-level source told Reuters last week.
Karatzas said the streamlining and restructuring of the National Bank group which involves mergers of subsidiary mortgage banks and insurance companies was proceeding smoothly.
He said he expected the merger of National Mortgage Bank and National Housing Bank to be completed before the end of 1997.

"I expect the parliament to pass a law facilitating mergers by early July at the latest," he said. "I think the merger of National Mortgage Bank and National Housing Bank will be completed by year-end."
National Mortgage Bank and National Housing Bank are subsidiaries of the National Bank.
National Investment Bank is designated to be the merchant bank of the group and will continue to invest in training its personnel and upgrading its infrastructure, he added.
Karatzas added that it was important for Greece's retail payments system called Dias to develop and expand with more commercial banks joining it.

"It is important to me that not just the National Bank but also the Greek banking sector become modern and prosper," said Karatzas. "The national economy and the banking sector need a fully developed retail payments system."
The National Bank and other large banks had invested a lot of money in the development of Dias and would like smaller commercial banks to gain access to Dias at a fair price.
"Fair pricing is the key word," he said. "Fair pricing can solve lingering problems." -- Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
